text:
The scoreboard made this look like a blowout, but through two periods it was a game VAN could have taken. At 16:56 of the second, Elias Pettersson scored shorthanded to make it 2-2, and NYR had been outchancing VAN by only a modest margin to that point. Then Tye Kartye scored 89 seconds later, at 18:25, and the game tilted for good.

The third period was the real separation. NYR out-chanced VAN 1.51 to 0.24 in expected goals, and the goals followed: Alexis Lafrenière on the power play at 1:04, Gabe Perreault at 5:57, and Will Cuylle at 15:22. Kevin Lankinen allowed 2.4 goals more than the 25 shots against him deserved, and he also stopped Eeli Tolvanen on an 18% look in the third. Cuylle's first goal, in the second period, came on a 3% chance, so the final margin owes a little to luck. Still, NYR's 3.64 expected goals to 1.62 says the better team won, and the model puts NYR's chance of deserving the win at 82%.

Kartye finished with two goals and was the first star, with Lafrenière and Perreault each adding a goal and an assist. J.T. Miller had two assists and 1.75 expected goals for against 0.27 against while he was on the ice. Dylan Garand faced 21 shots and allowed two. VAN's best moments came from Pettersson's shorthanded goal and Jake DeBrusk's snap shot on a 4% chance, but they won only 19 of 50 faceoffs and never held the puck long enough to answer in the third.
